01 / THE CHALLENGE

The challenge

Clinical documentation competes for the same time and attention as patient care. Before expanding the product, the workflow needed to be tested in real consultations, with clear measures of accuracy and speed.

02 / THE APPROACH

The approach

Designed and ran an 11-week pilot at Tulip Hospital across 371 outpatient consultations. The product combined differential diagnosis with clinical documentation, with doctors reviewing and correcting the generated notes.

03 / WHAT CHANGED

What changed

11-week pilot at Tulip Hospital across 371 consultations. Measured in the final 3 days: 91% note accuracy, about 20% less documentation time. These results followed changes made during the pilot; sustained institutional adoption and revenue were not established.

IN THE DETAILS

Pilot setting

Tulip Hospital · Outpatient doctors · Differential diagnosis plus clinical documentation · 11 weeks.

IN THE DETAILS

Improving the product during the pilot

I kept improving the product through the 11 weeks based on what doctors corrected. When I went through the corrected notes, 60% of the revisions came from two things: how our templates mapped to the hospital's record fields, and specialty terminology. I changed the templates and the field mapping while the pilot was still running. The accuracy and time figures come from the last 3 days, after those changes.

IN THE DETAILS

What the accuracy measure means

The 91% figure describes note accuracy against physician-reviewed documentation during the final 3 days. It is not a measure of diagnostic accuracy or independent clinical certification.

THE TAKEAWAY

A useful AI workflow needs more than a convincing demo. It needs a feedback loop that connects real usage, quality and time saved.
